approaches.name: Lateral para-olecranon triceps-on approach
approaches.region: posterior lateral elbow and distal humerus
approaches.corridor: Anconeus fascial split lateral to ulna with subperiosteal anconeus reflection and limited medial triceps split

sources.title: Surgical approaches for ORIF of intra-articular distal humerus fractures in adults
Comparison of outcomes after triceps split versus sparing surgery for extra-articular distal humerus fractures

procedure_applications.condition: Elbow arthroplasty is planned with preservation of the triceps insertion
An extra-articular or simple intra-articular fracture can be reduced without olecranon osteotomy

positioning.text: Position lateral or prone with arm supported, elbow freely flexed, and posterior humerus accessible for imaging.

setup.text: Plan arthroplasty versus fixation, ulnar-nerve handling, possible medial window, and immediate conversion to olecranon osteotomy if articular access proves inadequate.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark humeral shaft, olecranon, subcutaneous ulna, medial epicondyle, and ulnar-nerve course.

incision.text: Use a posterior incision from the middle-distal humeral junction to ulnar diaphysis, curving around rather than directly over olecranon tip.

superficial_interval.text: Raise full-thickness fasciocutaneous flaps, identify ulnar nerve proximally, release through cubital tunnel to first motor branch, and preserve perineural vessels.

deep_interval.text: Split anconeus fascia 1 cm lateral to ulna, continue lateral to triceps insertion then into medial triceps, and reflect anconeus/capsule subperiosteally from proximal ulna and lateral column.

layers.text: Skin, full-thickness flap, anconeus fascia, subperiosteal anconeus-capsule layer, limited triceps split, then posterior distal humerus.

structures_encountered.text: Ulnar nerve, triceps, anconeus, posterior capsule, collateral ligaments, distal humerus, olecranon, and proximal ulna are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Ulnar nerve and FCU motor branch, radial nerve proximally, collateral ligaments, triceps/anconeus blood supply, and articular cartilage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Never tension the mobilized ulnar nerve with a clipped sling; at closure leave it tension free and away from metalwork and sutures.

retraction_hazards.text: Move the triceps-on sleeve gently and avoid sustained ulnar-nerve traction or circumferential soft-tissue stripping.

exposure.text: Preserves triceps insertion while exposing posterior articular surface; medial window supports dual plating and conversion to osteotomy is straightforward.

limitations.text: Ulna preparation for arthroplasty and complex multifragmentary articular visualization are more difficult than through extensile osteotomy.

extensions.text: Add medial paratricipital window, reflect collateral origins for arthroplasty dislocation, or convert to planned olecranon osteotomy.

indications.text: Use primarily for total elbow arthroplasty and selectively for extra-articular or simple intra-articular distal-humerus fractures.

relative_contraindications.text: Choose an olecranon osteotomy or other extensile exposure for highly comminuted articular fractures requiring complete visualization.

implant_implications.text: Supports posterior/lateral and medial plating through separate windows; document final ulnar-nerve location and prevent implant contact.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use AP, lateral, and oblique views to verify column alignment, joint congruity, implant containment, and arthroplasty position.

closure.text: Repair reflected collateral ligaments when used, restore anconeus fascia and triceps split, and place ulnar nerve tension free away from sutures and implants.

complications.text: Complications include ulnar neuropathy, instability after ligament release, stiffness, triceps weakness, infection, nonunion, and implant failure.

bailouts.text: Convert early to olecranon osteotomy when direct articular control is insufficient rather than forcing the triceps-on window.

questions.question: What insertion remains intact?
questions.answer: The triceps insertion on the ulna.

questions.question: Where is the anconeus fascial split?
questions.answer: About 1 cm lateral to the subcutaneous ulnar border.

questions.question: What is the principal conversion?
questions.answer: Olecranon osteotomy for more articular access.

approaches.name: Medial approach to the distal humerus
approaches.corridor: Medial epicondylar exposure with ulnar-nerve mobilization and flexor-pronator split anterior to MCL

sources.title: Surgical approaches for ORIF of intra-articular distal humerus fractures in adults
Capitellum fractures: should the collateral ligament be repaired primarily?

procedure_applications.condition: An isolated medial epicondyle avulsion or rare medial trochlear fracture requires direct access

positioning.text: Position supine or lateral with elbow flexed and medial elbow accessible for nerve release and fluoroscopy.

setup.text: Plan ulnar-nerve management, MCL preservation, and fixation direction; document baseline ulnar-nerve function.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark medial epicondyle, medial supracondylar ridge, flexor-pronator mass, olecranon, and ulnar-nerve groove.

incision.text: Center incision on medial epicondyle, extending proximally along supracondylar ridge and distally with flexor-pronator mass.

superficial_interval.text: Protect the posterior medial antebrachial cutaneous branch, then identify ulnar nerve from medial septum through groove to FCU heads.

deep_interval.text: Mobilize ulnar nerve gently; for trochlea split flexor-pronator mass anterior to MCL, elevate muscle/capsule from ridge, and reflect capsule anterior to MCL.

layers.text: Skin, sensory-nerve plane, ulnar-nerve plane, flexor-pronator fascia, capsule, then medial distal humerus.

structures_encountered.text: Medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve, ulnar nerve, FCU heads, flexor-pronator origin, MCL, medial epicondyle, and trochlea are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Ulnar nerve and FCU motor branch, medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve, MCL, brachial artery/median nerve anteriorly, and trochlear cartilage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Keep flexor-pronator split anterior to MCL and preserve the first FCU motor branch during any ulnar-nerve transposition.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid prolonged traction on ulnar nerve and anterior lever retraction toward brachial artery and median nerve.

exposure.text: Exposes medial epicondyle and, with protected flexor-pronator/capsular extension, medial trochlea.

limitations.text: Isolated approach does not provide broad lateral-column or complete articular visualization.

extensions.text: Extend proximally along medial column or combine with posterior/lateral exposure while preserving MCL and nerve.

indications.text: Use for isolated medial epicondyle avulsion and selected isolated medial trochlear fractures.

relative_contraindications.text: Choose a posterior extensile approach for bicondylar or complex complete-articular patterns.

implant_implications.text: Place fixation clear of ulnar nerve and joint; repair any MCL/flexor-pronator detachment securely.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use AP, lateral, oblique, and trochlear views to confirm reduction, screw trajectory, and joint containment.

closure.text: Repair capsule and flexor-pronator origin, ensure MCL stability, and leave ulnar nerve tension free with final position documented.

complications.text: Complications include ulnar neuropathy, sensory neuroma, valgus instability, stiffness, heterotopic ossification, nonunion, and symptomatic hardware.

bailouts.text: Add posterior or lateral exposure when fracture visualization is incomplete rather than compromising MCL or neurovascular structures.

questions.question: Which cutaneous branch often crosses the incision?
questions.answer: The posterior branch of the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve.

questions.question: What must the operative report document?
questions.answer: How the ulnar nerve was protected and its final location.

approaches.name: Posterior paratricipital approach to the distal humerus
approaches.corridor: Medial and lateral windows around intact triceps insertion with posterior humeral elevation

sources.title: Surgical approaches for ORIF of intra-articular distal humerus fractures in adults
Outcomes for Type 13C1 and 13C2 fractures using the paratricipital approach

procedure_applications.condition: An extra-articular or simple intra-articular distal-humerus fracture can be fixed through triceps-sparing medial and lateral windows

positioning.text: Position lateral or prone with arm supported, elbow freely flexed, and posterior humerus accessible to fluoroscopy.

setup.text: Review articular comminution and plan dual-column plating, ulnar-nerve handling, and conversion to osteotomy if visualization is inadequate.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark humeral shaft, olecranon, medial/lateral epicondyles, ulnar nerve, and subcutaneous ulna.

incision.text: Use posterior incision from middle-distal humeral junction to ulnar diaphysis, avoiding direct placement over olecranon tip.

superficial_interval.text: Raise full-thickness flaps and create an ulnar window after releasing and protecting ulnar nerve to first FCU motor branch.

deep_interval.text: Mobilize triceps from lateral septum and posterior humerus, elevate anconeus posterolaterally, and move intact triceps sleeve medially or laterally for two-window access.

layers.text: Skin, full-thickness flaps, medial ulnar-nerve window and lateral triceps-anconeus window, then posterior distal humerus.

structures_encountered.text: Ulnar nerve, triceps, anconeus, medial/lateral columns, posterior capsule, MCL posterior band, and LUCL are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Ulnar nerve, radial nerve proximally, anterior MCL band, LUCL, triceps insertion, and articular cartilage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Only posterior MCL band and posterolateral capsule may be released for exposure; preserve anterior MCL and LUCL.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid sustained ulnar-nerve traction and excessive displacement of intact triceps sleeve.

exposure.text: Provides medial and lateral column access without triceps detachment or olecranon osteotomy and retains olecranon as reduction template.

limitations.text: Articular visualization is limited for highly comminuted C3 patterns compared with olecranon osteotomy.

extensions.text: Release only posterior capsular bands or convert to olecranon osteotomy when safe direct articular visualization remains inadequate.

indications.text: Use for extra-articular and simple intra-articular distal-humerus fractures, including selected C1-C2 patterns.

relative_contraindications.text: Prefer transolecranon or another extensile approach for severe articular comminution requiring complete visualization.

implant_implications.text: Supports orthogonal or parallel dual plating through two windows while preserving triceps insertion; keep ulnar nerve off implants.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use AP, lateral, and oblique views to verify articular reduction, column alignment, and screw containment where direct view is limited.

closure.text: Repair released capsule, restore anconeus/triceps fascial intervals, and leave ulnar nerve tension free away from sutures and metalwork.

complications.text: Complications include ulnar neuropathy, stiffness, limited articular reduction, nonunion, infection, heterotopic ossification, and fixation failure.

bailouts.text: Convert to olecranon osteotomy if direct reduction cannot be verified through the two windows.

questions.question: Which MCL portion may be released?
questions.answer: The posterior band, while preserving the anterior band.
